decisions.statement: A change may name paths moved on disk rather than written from a body.
A change naming a move and no body is a change rather than nothing asked for.
A path moved goes by one rename rather than by a write and a taking away.
A path moved that the base commit has is committed as the rename that path made.
A path moved that no commit has moves on disk and is committed nowhere.
A body judged where a move lands is the body that move started from.
A body written at the path a move lands at is written after that move.
A landing moving a path from another path works the change out itself.
Those paths move after the index is settled and before the commit.
A move that throws puts back in reverse the moves made before that move.
A commit that throws puts back every move made for that commit.
A landing that throws has moved nothing.
A caller taking a path away may move that path aside rather than unlink it.
The name a path is moved aside to is that path with the process's number and a word after it.
A path moved aside is put back where it came from or unlinked, at the caller's word.
A move aside that throws partway puts back every path moved aside before it.
Putting back a path whose aside name has gone leaves that path alone.
A folder left with nothing by a path moved away is cleared off the disk.
The paths a move aside took are answered, so the folder those paths empty is cleared.
A path moved away that something still imports refuses the change unwritten.

definition: a body a landing moves from one path to another rather than writing it and taking the old away
